T448 (a killed regression run leaves its fixtures in the live tree) — closed. The defect class: tools/regression-*.sh scripts write fixture files into the LIVE checkout (one of which is the tracked AGENTS.md) and remove them only in an EXIT trap. tools/runner SIGKILLs on wall/CPU/RSS/progress guards, and SIGKILL bypasses traps entirely — so a SIGKILLed run leaves every fixture it had touched sitting in the tree. Two bad consequences: (1) the residue can be staged by the next `git add -A` any console runs — the same mechanism that staged 1659 files in the T445 incident, arriving by a different door; (2) the residue (a deliberately non-conforming findings file or a deliberately volatile citation) corrupts claimlint readings while it sits there. Found by claude-opus-5/orcha on 2026-08-18 while deriving the answer key for the T447 race; verified at HEAD 9c08584.

THE FIX (delivered, two scripts plus the startup-check plumbing). Every regression script that creates live-tree fixtures now has THREE layers of cleanup, in increasing order of load-bearing-ness:

  Layer 1 — INLINE cleanup at the end of each arm (the pre-existing common path; unchanged where it was correct). Arm 1 of regression-argus-doctor.sh still restores AGENTS.md from $SEED_BAK inline at the end of its body.

  Layer 2 — TRAP on EXIT/INT/TERM/HUP (was EXIT only, so SIGKILL bypassed it AND so did any uncaught signal that interrupted inline cleanup). Every fixture path is now in a named cleanup() function so the trap handles signals uniformly. tools/runner's SIGKILL on the wall/CPU/RSS/progress guards is routine in this fleet, and SIGKILL cannot be trapped at all — so this layer is the safety net for signals that DO let the trap run.

  Layer 3 — STARTUP CHECK (the load-bearing half). Each script refuses to run if any of its fixtures is already present. SIGKILL cannot be trapped at all, so the only honest guard against a SIGKILLed run leaving residue is 'refuse to start if anything looks like residue'. The script refuses with RC=3 and names the stale path; the operator removes the file by hand after confirming it is fixture-shaped (and not, e.g., a real edit by another console — T445 staged 1659 files this way, and silently overwriting a stray fixture would re-enable exactly the same mechanism by hiding the evidence that a run was killed).

RECURSION FIX (a defect in the prior console's diff, found during T448.2 by running the script): the kill-survival self-check arm re-invokes `sh "$0"` to exercise the startup check, but the recursive invocation ran the WHOLE suite and therefore re-planted the same fixture in arm 5, recursing until the OS killed the test — T448.2 observed a 120s timeout. Fixed by an env-var guard (SKIP_KILL_SURVIVAL=1) that lets the recursive invocation run the startup check and the trap but skips the arms section. The same pattern was missing from regression-claim-lifecycle.sh and is added there too: CLAIMLINT_SKIP_KILL_SURVIVAL=1 set on the recursive invocations, with the same early-exit guard before the arms.
